evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 3.3.3: accūsātōribus frīgidissimīs ūtitur, lukewarm (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Brut. 178: nimis lentus in dīcendō et paene frīgidus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically of a person without warmth or zeal, lukewarm, indifferent. The construction with in and the accusative is Traupman’s; we have found no classical instance of it.

evidence: Hor. S. 2.1.62: majōrum nē quis amīcus frīgore tē feriat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A cold reception, loss of favour; Lewis & Short finds the sense perhaps not before Augustus.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
